advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the bisect payload with the full CI gate set (or document that it deliberately covers only the check+default-suite subset) so a responder is not misled when the redness came from pip-audit / config-check / integration tier.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:41-45: BISECT_PAYLOAD = ( "uv sync --locked --extra dev " '&& PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make check ' '&& PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test' )

_build-and-test.yml runs additional gates not in the payload: 'uv lock --check', pip-audit, config-check, and the integration tier (tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:71-72 lists 'default test suite' AND 'integration tier' as shared gates)
Makefile:207-208: 'test:' runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` — integration tier excluded
advisory.finding: The bisect reproduction payload (`uv sync --locked --extra dev && make check && make test`) is a strict subset of what the CI `build-and-test` reusable actually gates. The reusable additionally runs `uv lock --check`, pip-audit, drift gates, `make config-check`, and the integration test tier (`pytest -m integration`). A scheduled run reddened by any of those gates would hand the responder a `git bisect run` recipe that reports 'good' at every commit and never converges on the culprit.
scenarios: A commit that breaks only the integration tier or trips pip-audit reddens the scheduled run; the responder pastes the recipe and every bisect step reports green, so the bisect terminates without identifying the bad commit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider whether the last-known-green lookup should be constrained to schedule/push events (or ancestry-checked) so the resolved lower bound is always an ancestor of the failing HEAD.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:72: query = f"branch={branch}&status=success&per_page=1" — filters only by branch+success, not by event type
scripts/main_health_report.py:172: f"git bisect start {head_sha} {good}" — feeds the resolved sha directly as the good bound
The green renderer names the current head_sha as the bound, but the red renderer trusts whatever run history returns with no ancestry check
advisory.finding: On a RED run, the last-known-green lower bound is the head_sha of the newest *successful* run of test.yml on the branch, which can be a `workflow_dispatch` run rather than a scheduled/push run. A manual dispatch can be run against an arbitrary ref/SHA that is not an ancestor of the current HEAD, in which case the emitted `git bisect start <bad> <good>` fails (git rejects a good commit that is not an ancestor of bad).
scenarios: Someone dispatches test.yml successfully against a topic-branch SHA or an old main SHA; the next red scheduled run resolves that non-ancestor SHA as `good`, and `git bisect start` errors out for the responder.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a resolve_last_green failure-mode case where `workflow_runs[0]` is a non-Mapping (e.g. `{"workflow_runs": [42]}`) and assert it yields ('','') rather than raising.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:90-92: `newest = runs[0]` then `if not isinstance(newest, Mapping): return "", ""` — a distinct branch from the KeyError/ValueError guard at lines 84-87

tests/unit/test_main_health_report.py:148-166: the failure-mode parametrization lists 'api error', 'empty history', 'malformed body', 'unexpected shape' — none supplies a non-Mapping run element, so the isinstance guard is never exercised
ABSENCE: were the `isinstance(newest, Mapping)` guard removed, `newest.get(...)` on a non-dict element would raise and violate the FAIL-SOFT-BY-CONTRACT docstring, yet no existing test would fail
advisory.finding: resolve_last_green's fail-soft branch for a non-Mapping newest run element (main_health_report.py:91-92) is untested; the parametrized failure-mode suite covers api-error, empty-history, malformed-body, and unexpected-shape, but not a run list whose first element is not a dict (e.g. {"workflow_runs": [42]}), which is a distinct code path guarding a documented fail-soft contract.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrize entry: ("non-mapping run element", {"stdout": '{"workflow_runs": [42]}'}) to test_every_lookup_failure_mode_fails_soft.
